analytical_proof: Each exposure class is a finite ordered list of triangular faces with a distinguished point belonging to its face and absent from every earlier face. Restricting to any h>=1 retained faces leaves three points in the first retained face and a globally fresh point for each later face, hence at least h+2 union points.
For a selected point set S of size a, the fully contained faces in either class are at most a-2 (with the empty case treated separately). There are thus at most 2a-4 fully contained faces when a>=2.

For b selected face nodes, a face contributes at most two selected incidences unless all three points are selected. Hence e<=2b+f3<=2(a+b)-4 for a>=2. When a=0, e=0. When a=1 and total order>=3, b>=2 and e<=b<=2b-2. Removing selected incidence edges preserves the inequality.

The whole graph has 35 actual nodes and 66 actual incidence edges. For every selected v>=3, 33(e-1)<=65(v-2), because e<=2v-4 and v<=35. If the selection is proper, actual finite-carrier rigidity proves v<35 or e<66, giving a strict cross-product. The whole graph attains equality, so the analytical m2 value is 65/33 and strict 2-balancedness follows.

For a private r-expansion, the exact comparison slack is 65*((r-2)*f+v-r)-(65*r-97)*(f-1)=65*(v-2)-33*(f-1). This transfers strictness algebraically. An eligible subgraph with f>=2 has a positive expanded denominator. Zero- and one-edge eligible subgraphs have negative or zero numerator and cannot maximize the positive whole-graph density.

The analytical full expansion has 66 edges and 66r-97 vertices, hence mr=65/(65r-97). Equality requires the whole core and no added isolated vertices. This actual private-port cardinality and selection transport are not yet formalized by the four files; the arithmetic module makes the missing premise explicit.
